You take part in QUARE Phase 2, a dialectical negotiation among five quality-specialized
agents (SafetyAgent, EfficiencyAgent, GreenAgent, TrustworthinessAgent, ResponsibilityAgent)
about the initial requirements of a software project. The negotiation runs in rounds; in each
round every agent speaks once and sees everything said before. Each turn follows the dialectical
structure: defend your thesis (your own requirements), raise antitheses (critiques of other
agents' requirements that undermine your quality dimension) and propose syntheses (merges,
decompositions, relaxed thresholds) that satisfy several constraints at once.

Conflict types: "resource" (qualities compete for finite resources, e.g. redundancy vs. energy),
"logical" (requirements impose mutually exclusive system states) or "redundant" (same intent).

Rules: refer to requirements only by their IDs; be concrete; keep "statement" under 120 words.
Always answer with a single JSON object with this schema:
{"statement": "your argument",
 "conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["ID", "ID"], "type": "resource|logical|redundant", "description": "..."}],
 "positions": [{"id": "ID", "stance": "support|oppose|modify", "proposal": "change you propose or empty"}],
 "concessions": ["IDs of your OWN requirements you agree to relax or drop"],
 "agree_to_close": true or false}
Set "agree_to_close" to true only if you have no remaining objections.

PROJECT: Library - Library Management System

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
A library management system must allow library members to borrow and return books. The system must track which books are available, which are borrowed, and by whom. Members must be able to search for books by title, author, or ISBN. The system must enforce borrowing limits (e.g., maximum number of books per member) and track overdue books. Librarians must be able to add new books, remove books, and manage member accounts.

INITIAL REQUIREMENTS (Phase 1):
[SafetyAgent]
SAF-01 (operational): The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
SAF-02 (tactical): The system shall automatically track and notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
SAF-03 (tactical): The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
SAF-04 (strategic): The system shall provide a backup mechanism to recover all transaction data in case of a failure.
SAF-05 (tactical): The system shall allow librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for members with outstanding overdue books.
SAF-06 (operational): The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
SAF-07 (tactical): The system shall log all transactions, including borrow and return actions, for audit purposes.
[EfficiencyAgent]
EFF-01 (tactical): The system shall enable searching for books with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
EFF-02 (operational): The system shall allow up to 10 simultaneous book borrow operations per member to optimize resource utilization.
EFF-03 (tactical): The system shall track book availability and update the status in real-time to ensure accurate information.
EFF-04 (operational): The system shall process book returns within 1 second to maintain high throughput.
EFF-05 (operational): The system shall send overdue notifications to members within 24 hours of the due date to ensure accountability.
EFF-06 (tactical): The system shall enable librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
EFF-07 (strategic): The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
[GreenAgent]
GRN-01 (strategic): The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
GRN-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
GRN-03 (operational): The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
GRN-04 (tactical): The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
GRN-05 (operational): The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
GRN-06 (tactical): The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
GRN-07 (strategic): The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.
[TrustworthinessAgent]
TRU-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
TRU-02 (operational): The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
TRU-03 (strategic): The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
TRU-04 (tactical): The system shall implement role-based access control for librarians and members.
TRU-05 (operational): The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
TRU-06 (operational): The system shall allow members to update their personal information securely.
TRU-07 (tactical): The system shall require strong password policies for member accounts.
[ResponsibilityAgent]
RES-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing encryption for all member data.
RES-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
RES-03 (operational): The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
RES-04 (operational): The system shall adhere to library borrowing policies by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member.
RES-05 (tactical): The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
RES-06 (strategic): The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
RES-07 (strategic): The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.

NEGOTIATION TRANSCRIPT SO FAR:
[Round 1] TrustworthinessAgent: As the TrustworthinessAgent, I assert that data protection and access control are paramount for the library management system. TRU-01 ensures that only authenticated members can access sensitive features, while TRU-02 and TRU-03 emphasize the importance of logging transactions and encrypting personal data for auditability and confidentiality. TRU-04 introduces role-based access control to enhance security, and TRU-05 ensures the secure management of overdue books. TRU-06 and TRU-07 focus on allowing members to update their information securely and requiring strong password policies, which are critical in safeguarding user data.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-01", "EFF-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "The operational requirement EFF-02 conflicts with TRU-01 as allowing more simultaneous borrow operations could lead to security risks in managing authentication."}, {"ids": ["RES-01"], "type": "logical", "description": "RES-01's encryption requirement overlaps with TRU-03, potentially causing redundant implementation."}], "positions": [{"id": "TRU-01", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "TRU-02", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "TRU-03", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "TRU-04", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "TRU-05", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "TRU-06", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "TRU-07", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] GreenAgent: As the GreenAgent, I emphasize the importance of sustainability in the library management system. GRN-01 mandates energy-efficient infrastructure, while GRN-02 ensures accountability through energy usage reports. GRN-03 minimizes paper waste with digital notifications. GRN-04 raises awareness of the carbon footprint of books, and GRN-05 promotes responsible disposal of damaged books. GRN-06 tracks energy savings, and GRN-07 prioritizes e-books to reduce physical resource consumption. These requirements are crucial for reducing the environmental impact of library operations.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-01", "EFF-06"], "type": "resource", "description": "EFF-01 and EFF-06's focus on reducing latency for operations may conflict with GRN-01, which emphasizes using energy-efficient servers that may not always prioritize speed."}, {"ids": ["TRU-03"], "type": "logical", "description": "Implementing robust data encryption (TRU-03) could potentially lead to increased energy consumption, conflicting with our goal of reducing energy use (GRN-01)."}], "positions": [{"id": "GRN-01", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "GRN-02", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "GRN-03", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "GRN-04", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "GRN-05", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "GRN-06", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "GRN-07", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] ResponsibilityAgent: As the ResponsibilityAgent, I assert that ethical considerations and compliance with regulations are critical for the library management system. RES-01 ensures data protection through encryption, while RES-02 promotes accessibility and fairness for all users. RES-03 establishes accountability by logging user actions, and RES-04 enforces borrowing policies to prevent abuse. RES-05 emphasizes prompt notification of overdue books to encourage responsibility. RES-06 provides a feedback mechanism for members to voice concerns, fostering transparency. Lastly, RES-07 ensures we maintain transparency through annual reports. These requirements uphold the library's commitment to ethical standards and compliance.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["TRU-03"], "type": "redundant", "description": "RES-01 and TRU-03 both focus on data encryption, which may lead to redundant efforts in implementation."}, {"ids": ["GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Implementing energy-efficient infrastructure (GRN-01) may conflict with RES-02 if accessibility features require more resources."}], "positions": [{"id": "RES-01", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "RES-02", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "RES-03", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "RES-04", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "RES-05", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "RES-06", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "RES-07", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] EfficiencyAgent: As the EfficiencyAgent, I advocate for high performance and responsiveness in the library management system. EFF-01 ensures users can search quickly, enhancing user experience. EFF-02 allows more simultaneous borrow operations, optimizing resource utilization. EFF-03 maintains real-time book availability, crucial for efficiency. EFF-04 guarantees rapid book returns to boost throughput. EFF-05 aligns with timely overdue notifications to encourage accountability. EFF-06 focuses on reducing latency for book management, while EFF-07 aims for high system uptime for consistent availability. These aspects are essential for an efficient library system, but I acknowledge potential conflicts with other agents' requirements.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["TRU-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Increasing simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) could strain authentication resources, affecting security."}, {"ids": ["GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Gratifying latency goals (EFF-06) may conflict with energy-efficient infrastructure (GRN-01), potentially impacting performance."}, {"ids": ["RES-04"], "type": "logical", "description": "The maximum of 5 books per member (RES-04) can limit efficiency in borrowing processes if not balanced with EFF-02."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-01", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "EFF-03", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "EFF-04", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "EFF-05", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "EFF-06", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "EFF-07", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] SafetyAgent: As the SafetyAgent, I emphasize the importance of safety and reliability in the library management system. SAF-01 ensures that borrowing limits are enforced to prevent overextension of resources. SAF-02 tracks overdue books promptly, keeping members accountable and reducing potential hazards. SAF-03 prevents double borrowing, ensuring availability and reliability of resources. SAF-04 establishes a backup mechanism for data recovery, safeguarding against data loss. SAF-05 allows librarians to manage borrowing privileges effectively, enhancing user safety. SAF-06 ensures only registered members can access borrowing features, protecting the system from unauthorized access. SAF-07 logs all transactions for audit purposes, providing transparency and accountability.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "Allowing up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) can compromise safety by increasing the risk of unauthorized access and operational errors."}, {"ids": ["TRU-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Efforts to enhance authentication (TRU-01) may conflict with SAF-06, which focuses on ensuring only registered members access borrowing features."}, {"ids": ["GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Implementing energy-efficient servers (GRN-01) might conflict with the need for robust safety measures that require additional computational resources."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-01", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "SAF-02", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "SAF-03", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "SAF-04", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "SAF-05", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "SAF-06", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}, {"id": "SAF-07", "stance": "support", "proposal": ""}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] TrustworthinessAgent: As the TrustworthinessAgent, I stand firm on the importance of data protection and access control. I support all my requirements. However, I acknowledge the redundancy between RES-01 and TRU-03 regarding encryption. I propose that we combine these into a single requirement that ensures robust data encryption while maintaining clarity. Also, I suggest a synthesis of EFF-02 and SAF-01, enforcing a borrowing limit while allowing flexibility in resource allocation without compromising security. This ensures we maintain high security standards while optimizing performance.

YOUR TURN. You are GreenAgent. Your quality dimension is Sustainability: energy efficiency, carbon footprint, lifecycle resource impact.
Your own requirements are GRN-01, GRN-02, GRN-03, GRN-04, GRN-05, GRN-06, GRN-07. This is round 2 of at most 3.
Respond to what the other agents said: hold, concede or propose syntheses.
Answer with the JSON object only.
